title: The Axis of Upheaval Goes to War
gist: China and Russia are helping Iran target US forces without entering the war, supplying satellite imagery, drones and missile expertise, while US allies were reluctant to back the campaign or help secure the Strait of Hormuz.

themes.theme: Chinese and Russian targeting support to Iran

insights.claim: Before the July 17 Iranian missile strike that killed three US soldiers at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, Tehran received high-resolution satellite images of the base from Chinese entities.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Chinese commercial and state satellite imagery is a live escalation channel; expect US pressure on Chinese space-imagery firms.

insights.claim: Russia fed Iran satellite intelligence that aided precision strikes: 14 Russian spy satellites passed over Prince Sultan Air Base two days before the March 27 attack that wounded 12 Americans.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Russia-Iran intelligence cooperation raises strike accuracy against Gulf bases and assets.
insights.quote: Two days before the March 27 attack

insights.claim: Russia has given Iran weapons and expertise, including drones upgraded on the Ukrainian battlefield, and Russian engineers are helping develop supersonic cruise missiles able to evade US and Israeli air defenses.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Raises the threat to regional air defence and sustains demand for layered interceptors.
insights.quote: Moscow has also provided Iran with weapons and military expertise

insights.claim: Russia and China support Iran with intelligence, military technology, components, and economic and diplomatic backing without joining the war, limiting their own costs and risks.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Expect adversaries to keep arming proxies at arm's length, so sanctions and escalation risk fall on third countries.

insights.claim: The Russia-China-Iran partners are fine-tuning cooperation to make partners more resilient and more dangerous to the US while limiting costs and risks.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Durable axis cooperation implies prolonged conflict and persistent energy-route risk.
insights.quote: They are fine-tuning their cooperation to make their partners more resilient—and more dangerous to the United States—while limiting costs and risks.

themes.theme: US alliance friction in the Iran war

insights.claim: Despite a vast network of allies and bases, many US partners were reluctant to associate with the Iran campaign, some denied specific military access for a time, and others publicly resisted calls to help secure the Strait of Hormuz.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Allied reluctance weakens the US ability to secure shipping lanes, a lasting risk premium for Hormuz-linked energy and freight.
insights.quote: Others publicly resisted U.S. calls to help secure the Strait of Hormuz.
